metaDescription: Six eufy robot vacuums from the slim 11S MAX to the 35,000 Pa C30, compared by mop style, dock design, carpet handling and long-term upkeep.
expertTake: The eufy E28 is the top pick because a detachable handheld cleaner turns the robot station into a spot cleaner for carpet stains. The C10 is the value pick, a slim laser robot with a bag dock. People with a small, tidy home should skip the hot-water flagships and buy the 11S MAX.
introParagraphs: This maker covers three distinct ideas under one name. The oldest is a thin, quiet robot with no mapping and no dock. The middle is a laser-guided robot with a bag dock, and the newest is a roller-mop station that also tackles allergens, stains or carpets.

That spread is why the model list can be confusing. A good choice starts with the job you want done, whether that is daily dust, wet floors or carpet spot cleaning, and then picks the cheapest model that actually does it.

products.name: eufy E28, 20,000 Pa, roller mop, detachable portable deep cleaner
products.description:
The E28 does something no other model in this guide does. A handheld deep cleaner lifts off the station, so the same machine that runs the floors on a schedule can also be carried to a stained sofa cushion or a pet accident on carpet. The robot side is a self-cleaning roller mop with HydroJet water delivery and carpet detection that raises suction on rugs.

It reaches 20,000 Pa, the same label as the E25 but below the C30, and the handheld costs more upkeep than a simple dock. Against the X10 Pro Omni it gains the portable tool and a roller instead of two spinning pads. For a family with toddlers or pets that stain carpet, the detachable cleaner is worth the price tier.

There are two machines to care for: the robot and the portable unit. Empty and rinse the portable tank after every use, dry its brush head, and keep the roller tray clean. Spare rollers and brush heads are the ongoing cost. Store the handheld on the dock so it is charged when the carpet accident happens, because a flat battery defeats the point.
products.bestFor: Homes where carpet stains and pet accidents are a regular event.
pros: Detachable handheld cleans stains off carpet and upholstery
Roller mop is rinsed with fresh water as it works
Carpet detection raises suction automatically
Station handles emptying and mop washing
cons: Two tools to clean and store
Handheld tank is small for big spills

products.name: eufy C30, 35,000 Pa, AeroTurbo multi-cyclone filtration
products.description:
The C30 is the suction flagship. AeroTurbo is a multi-cyclone filter stack that spins dust out of the airflow so the filter clogs more slowly, which matters because a clogged filter, not the motor, is why suction fades after a few months. It is aimed at carpet and pet hair, with a mop for the hard-floor follow-up.

The 35,000 Pa label is the highest in the group, though it is a peak rating and brush design still decides carpet results. Against the E28 it trades the handheld cleaner for raw airflow and sits at a lower price tier than the S2 line. If your home is mostly thick rugs, this is the sensible suction pick.

Cyclone filters are only useful if cleaned. Empty the dust chamber often, wash the cyclone stack when the app flags it, and let it dry before refitting. Brush heads and filters are ongoing costs, and the large motor is audible in full boost. A home office with calls during the day will want the quieter standard mode and boost only on carpet.
products.bestFor: Carpeted homes with shedding pets that need maximum airflow.
pros: Multi-cyclone stack slows filter clogging
Highest suction label in the lineup
Built for pet hair and carpet
Lower price tier than the S2 line
cons: Peak suction is loud at full boost
No handheld cleaner like the E28

products.name: eufy S2, 30,000 Pa, electrolyzed water, HydroJet 2.0 roller
products.description:
The S2 is the allergy and hygiene model. It generates electrolyzed water on board to wet the roller, and the maker claims strong germ reduction on hard floors and dust-mite removal on carpet, so treat those as vendor claims rather than lab results. A sealed filter path is meant to keep fine allergens from returning to the room.

It sits at a higher tier than the C30 and has less raw suction at 30,000 Pa, because the money goes to the water system and filtration. The HydroJet 2.0 roller is a step beyond the roller on the E28. For a household with a baby on the floor or someone with allergies, the cleaner water system is the reason to buy.

The electrolysis cell is a part that scales in hard water, so descale on the maker's schedule and rinse the roller tray. Allergen filters are replaceable and should be changed on time, otherwise the filtration claim means nothing. Because the cell and filters are brand-specific, buy spares early rather than when the app complains.
products.bestFor: Allergy-sensitive homes and families with crawling babies.
pros: Electrolyzed water made on board for the roller
Allergen filter stack for fine dust
HydroJet 2.0 roller scrubs hard floors
Strong 30,000 Pa label for carpet
cons: Germ and mite figures are vendor claims
Higher price tier than the C30

products.name: eufy X10 Pro Omni, 8,000 Pa, dual spinning mops, 12 mm auto-lift
products.description:
The X10 Pro Omni is the older, pad-based station in the group. Two spinning mop pads press against the floor and lift 12 mm when the robot crosses carpet, then the dock washes them with fresh water and dries them with 45 C air. No-go zones and carpet detection come with the app.

Its 8,000 Pa is a fraction of the newer models, and the pad design is a step behind the roller on the E28 for dried stains. It costs less than the E-series because the technology is older. The 12 mm lift is generous enough for thin rugs, so it remains a good pick for mixed flooring.

Pads are consumables that need replacing every few months, and a heated dry cycle keeps the dock from smelling. Wipe the pad bay and rinse the tanks regularly, since the station's filter screens clog with lint from the pads. A weekly glance at the drain screen prevents the slow water flow that ends in an error code.
products.bestFor: Mixed floors where light wet cleaning and rugs share the plan.
pros: Dual pads lift 12 mm over carpet
Pads washed and dried at 45 C
No-go zones and carpet detection
Lower price tier than the E-series
cons: Pads smear dried spills more than a roller

products.name: eufy C10, self-empty station with 3 L bag, 2.85 in slim, LiDAR
products.description:
The C10 gets the basics right. A laser scanner maps the rooms, the body is only 2.85 in high and a 3 L bag dock empties the bin automatically for about eight weeks. It is a slim robot that keeps most of the convenience of the pricier models.

It has no mop and no pad washing, which is why it costs less than the X10 Pro Omni. Against the 11S MAX it adds mapping and a dock, and the 3 L bag is big enough to ignore for two months in a small home. If your floors are mostly hard and you mop by hand, this is the pragmatic choice.

Bag replacement is the running cost. Check the dock filter every few weeks, wipe the dock port and rinse the dustbin if you open it. The slim body fits under most furniture, but the laser turret is the tallest part, so measure the sofa gap. The 3 L bag is also easy to swap one-handed, which matters for owners with limited grip strength.
products.bestFor: Hard-floor homes that want mapping and a dock without mop hardware.
pros: Bag dock lasts about eight weeks
2.85 in body fits under furniture
LiDAR mapping and room control
Lowest tier among the docked models
cons: Laser turret adds height at the top

products.name: eufy 11S MAX, 2.85 in slim, BoostIQ, 100 min runtime
products.description:
The 11S MAX is the thin, quiet classic. At 2.85 in it glides under beds, and BoostIQ raises suction within about 1.5 seconds when it meets carpet. Runtime is up to 100 minutes on hardwood, and the maker rates it for hard floors up to medium-pile carpet.

It has no map, no dock and no mop, so you empty the bin and schedule by remote or button. Next to the C10 it loses navigation and automation, but it costs less and runs quieter. A studio or bedroom owner who wants daily crumbs removed will not miss the rest.

Care is the old-fashioned routine: empty the bin, rinse the filter, snip hair from the roller and replace the side brush. With no dock there is no bag cost, so the running bill is the lowest in the lineup. It is also the model that survives longest in a drawer between uses, since there is no water in it to go stale.
products.bestFor: Studios and bedrooms that need quiet daily crumb removal.
pros: 2.85 in body reaches under beds
BoostIQ adds suction on carpet within 1.5 s
Quiet running
No bag or water parts to buy
cons: Bin must be emptied by hand

buyingCriteria.explanation: The E28 and S2 use a roller rinsed with fresh water, and the X10 Pro Omni uses two spinning pads. A roller picks up dried spills and a pad mostly dampens them. If you mop weekly, choose the roller, and if you mop monthly, the pad is enough.

Carpet is the home of most bad reviews. A robot that cannot climb the rug edge or that wets the pile ends up parked in the cupboard within a month, which is the commonest way a good machine turns into a wasted purchase. The X10 Pro Omni lifts its pads 12 mm, the E28 detects carpet and boosts suction, and the 11S MAX uses BoostIQ. Thick shag defeats all of them, so be honest about your floors before choosing.
The C30 uses a multi-cyclone stack and the S2 pairs electrolyzed water with an allergen filter. Both aim at fine dust. Treat germ and mite percentages as vendor claims and change filters on schedule.
The C10 bag lasts about eight weeks from 3 L, and the 11S MAX has no bag at all. The mop stations add tanks to clean. A dock saves time only if you will keep it clean.
The C10 and 11S MAX are both 2.85 in tall, which clears most bed frames. The flagships stand taller. Measure the gap beneath your lowest piece, and allow a margin.
The E28 alone includes a detachable deep cleaner. It earns its place only if carpet stains or pet accidents are common. Otherwise it is extra weight and extra upkeep.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mop and carpet design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rollers, spinning pads and lift heights. The E28 and S2 lead on wet cleaning, and the X10 Pro Omni leads on rug lift. Models with no mop were judged on dry cleaning only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the filter claims, such as the C30 multi-cyclone and the S2 allergen stack. Vendor percentages were not treated as proof. A filter that is easy to wash scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dock and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted bags, pads, rollers and tanks. The 11S MAX has none of those, while the E28 has two tools. Convenience was weighed against upkeep.

howWeEvaluated.title: Physical fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared heights such as 2.85 in on the C10 and 11S MAX. Clearance decides where a robot can work. Taller flagships were marked down for low furniture.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed repeated owner reports on app connection, dock jams and carpet handling. Patterns outweighed single complaints. Older models were checked for parts supply.

cards.label: Pads
cards.text: The X10 Pro Omni spins two pads that lift 12 mm over rugs. They are cheaper to replace but smear stubborn stains.

howToChoose.note: Choose a roller if you mop weekly, and pads if mixed floors and occasional mopping are the rule.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Auto carpet detection, a suction boost, a mop that lifts or detaches and a brush that does not wrap. Check the maker's pile-height rating.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The C30 offers the most airflow and the E28 adds a handheld for stains. The X10 Pro Omni lifts its pads 12 mm for thin rugs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have carpet stains, allergies or heavy shedding. The E28, S2 and C30 each solve one of those directly.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have hard floors and mop by hand. The C10 or 11S MAX covers dry cleaning at a lower tier.

maintenance.task: Empty and rinse the portable tank
maintenance.why: The E28 handheld holds dirty water that smells quickly. Rinse it and leave the lid off.
Wound hair slows the roller and strains the motor. Cut it free along the roller groove.

maintenance.task: Wash the cyclone stack or filter
maintenance.why: Fine dust blocks airflow on the C30 and S2. Let the parts dry fully before refitting.
A full bag cuts suction and the dock's pull. Replace earlier in a home with pets.

maintenance.task: Descale electrolysis cell and water lines
maintenance.why: Hard water scales the S2 cell and the pumps on station models. Use the maker's descaler.

faq.q: Which eufy is best for pet hair?
faq.a: The C30 gives the most airflow for carpet, and the E28 adds a handheld for accidents. Both use brush designs aimed at hair. Check the roller weekly regardless.

faq.q: Is the electrolyzed water claim real?
faq.a: The S2 produces it on board, but the percentages for germs and mites are the maker's claims. Treat them as marketing until independent data appears. The roller and filter are the proven parts.

faq.q: Do I need a mop station?
faq.a: Only if you mop weekly. A station like the X10 Pro Omni saves effort but adds tanks and pads. The C10 covers dry work and costs less.

faq.q: Can these robots handle thick carpet?
faq.a: Carpet detection helps with medium pile. Thick shag defeats pads and rollers. The C30 is the strongest of the group for rugs.

faq.q: How long does the C10 bag last?
faq.a: The maker quotes about eight weeks from the 3 L bag. A shedding pet shortens it. Check at one month.

faq.q: Is the 11S MAX still worth buying?
faq.a: For a bedroom or studio, yes, because it is quiet and has no consumables. It has no map and no dock. Larger homes need the C10 or above.
